answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Signed royalty statement history from a publisher flips the bet — royalties a publisher paid out over years — and the mirror lands on the attacker instead. Even a well-funded farm hits a wall here, since royalties a publisher paid out over years takes calendar time as well as money — and the harbor is that time is the one resource a farm cannot print. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the mesa of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
